To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) general trait ratings are moderately stable over time and across situations; (2) trait variability is not well estimated by self-ratings; (3) general trait ratings correlate with a weighted average across situations; (4) the weights are not uniform across situations; (5) general trait ratings do not correlate with the variance of ratings across situations.

(1) the average of self-ratings for a trait across a large set of situations is a good indicator of the person’s general self-rating for that trait, and (2) the average of daily self-ratings for that trait over a short period is also a good indicator of a general self-rating for the trait.
(1) people are generally accurate in their judgments of their personality trait scores, but (2) they are generally inaccurate in judging their personality trait variability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between personality self-ratings and behavior in a wide variety of specific situations.
the relationship of two personality variables, Conscientiousness (C) and Outgoingness (O), as they are manifested in self-ratings.
the question of whether people can accurately judge how much they vary on personality dimensions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
personality traits, as measured by self-ratings, are relatively consistent over time and across different situations, but that variability in these traits is not accurately assessed.
the results of these studies support the general hypothesis that self-ratings of personality are valid measures of the individual’s personality.
general personality traits are relatively stable and consistent over time and across situations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the general self-ratings are fairly consistent across time and situations, and that the variability in the general ratings is a function of the consistency of the general ratings across time and situations.
personality is relatively stable over time and across situations.
personality traits are stable, but that people are inconsistent in their ratings of their own traits.
The main takeaway from our work is that

people are generally good at estimating the degree to which they vary in personality traits across situations, but they do not accurately estimate the extent to which they are different from one another in these traits.
people are generally consistent, but not always.
people are not very good at assessing the extent of variability in their behavior across situations. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
